why: This is a named computer-science education framework specifying seven practices, not a general explanatory theory of learning.

The candidate applies the canonical principle of Autonomy by recommending meaningful learner choice, decision-making, self-advocacy, and teacher practices that support voluntary control within structured K-12 learning environments.
The seven practices are the named K-12 Computer Science Framework's instructional framework, not a general learning theory.
name: K-12 Computer Science Framework
product_description: A framework developed by ACM, CSTA, Code.org, and collaborating experts that defines core practices and concepts for K-12 computer science education.

why: The K-16 Square is a named cross-sector education-policy framework developed by state education leaders and partner organizations, not a general theory of learning.
name: The K-16 Square
product_description: A K-16 education-system alignment framework drafted by state education CEOs with the National Association of System Heads and The Education Trust to coordinate standards for graduation, college admission, teaching, and teacher preparation.

why: K12-KGraph is a named, reusable curriculum knowledge-graph dataset rather than a general instructional element or teaching method.
name: K12-KGraph
product_description: A heterogeneous, curriculum-aligned knowledge graph extracted and expert-verified from official Chinese People's Education Press K–12 mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology textbooks, created by Hao Liang et al.

why: K12-Bench is a named benchmark dataset rather than a reusable instructional element or teaching design.
name: K12-Bench
product_description: K12-Bench is a 23,640-item multi-select benchmark dataset created by Hao Liang et al. for evaluating large language models' structural understanding of K–12 curricula.

why: K12-Train is a named curriculum-grounded QA dataset and synthesis pipeline for training educational language models, not a reusable instructional element.
name: K12-Train
product_description: K12-Train is a knowledge-graph-guided dataset and generation pipeline by Hao Liang et al. that produces validated text and multimodal K–12 STEM question-answer samples for supervised fine-tuning.

why: This is a domain-specific collection and use of software and hardware digital tools for learners to create and explore, rather than a distinct instructional element or single product.
This frames K-12 AI education as an emerging subject field and calls for curricula, pedagogies, and technologies, but it does not propose a general explanatory theory of learning or teaching.
K1/K2 is a study-specific classification of multiple-choice assessment items, not a general explanatory theory of learning or teaching.
